analysis.summary: DIRT argues that testing tools built for mature databases fit early-stage systems badly, and integrates the testing framework into the DBMS itself so that random testing evolves with the system and false positives are reduced by construction. It introduces generation actions, an abstraction that lets database developers rather than testing experts state correctness properties, and defines five oracles as sequences of them. Evaluated on Turso, an actively developed SQLite-compatible engine, it found 23 unique confirmed bugs.
analysis.narrative: DIRT takes SQLancer as both its point of departure and its baseline: three of its five oracles are reimplementations of SQLancer's, expressed as generation actions, and it explicitly declines to modify SQLancer itself, arguing that integrating a new DBMS into it is too laborious for a system under active development. It is careful to say that outperforming SQLancer on Turso does not mean it has better generators or oracles.
